def compute_ranks(vals):

def compute_ranks(vals):
    # Sort values with original indices
    indexed = sorted(list(enumerate(vals)), key=lambda x: x[1])
    n = len(vals)
    ranks = [0.0] * n
    i = 0
    while i < n:
        j = i
        while j < n and indexed[j][1] == indexed[i][1]:
            j += 1
        # Ties from i to j-1
        # Ranks are 1-based: indices i+1 to j
        avg_rank = ( (i + 1) + j ) / 2.0
        for k in range(i, j):
            ranks[indexed[k][0]] = avg_rank
        i = j
    return ranks

y_ranks = compute_ranks(y_vals)
x_ranks = compute_ranks(x_vals)

# Population covariance: sum((yr - mean_yr) * (xr - mean_xr)) / N

mean_xr = statistics.mean(x_ranks)
n = len(y_ranks)
cov = sum((y_ranks[i] - mean_yr) * (x_ranks[i] - mean_xr) for i in range(n)) / n
result = round(cov, 6)
